help.title: Nexora Desktop Manual
help.subtitle: Quick reference guide

intro.description: Nexora Desktop is a native multiplatform application for professional media processing. It brings the power of the Nexora server pipeline directly to your workstation, with zero cloud dependencies.
intro.quickStartDesc: Go to Library → drag a video file → click Reprocess → select a profile → monitor in Queue → review results in Asset Detail.

features.transcodingDesc: FFmpeg with GPU acceleration (NVENC, AMF, QSV) or CPU (libx264)
features.vmafDesc: Perceptual quality score 0-100 for each job
features.profilesDesc: Broadcast HD/SD, Web HD/4K, Social, Proxy
features.gpuAutoDesc: Automatic detection of NVIDIA, AMD and Intel
features.offline: Fully offline processing — no internet required
features.vmaf: Active VMAF quality scoring with per-profile thresholds

intro.architecture: Built with Tauri 2.x (Rust) for the native shell, React 19 for the UI, and a Node.js sidecar for media orchestration. SQLite stores all metadata locally.

dashboard.title: Dashboard — System Overview
dashboard.desc: The Dashboard shows your system health at a glance: total assets, jobs completed today, and average VMAF score.
dashboard.stat1: Total Assets — all media files in your library
dashboard.stat2: Jobs Today — completed jobs in the last 24 hours
dashboard.stat3: Average VMAF — mean quality score of recent outputs
dashboard.recentJobs: Recent Jobs — click any job to open its Asset Detail
dashboard.tip2: Click any job in the Recent Jobs list to jump to Asset Detail.
dashboard.tip3: The VMAF Distribution bar shows quality tiers at a glance.

library.title: Library — Asset Management
library.desc: The Library is your media repository. Ingest files via drag-and-drop or file dialog, then manage, preview, and reprocess them.
library.dragDrop: Drag & drop files from anywhere on your OS
library.gridList: Toggle between Grid and List views
library.searchFilter: Search by filename and filter by status
library.reprocess: Click any asset to reprocess with a different profile
library.tip1: Supported formats: MP4, MKV, MOV, MXF, AVI, WebM, TS, M2TS.
library.tip2: Hover over a grid card to reveal Open and Play buttons.
library.tip3: The view mode (Grid/List) is remembered between sessions.
library.deleteConfirmDesc: Diálogo de confirmação em dois passos. Primeiro confirma a remoção do asset; segundo pergunta se quer apagar o ficheiro processado do disco.

queue.title: Queue — Job Monitoring
queue.desc: The Queue shows all jobs in real time. Watch the 8-stage pipeline visualizer, approve quarantined jobs, and retry failures.
queue.quarantine: Quarantined jobs appear in Pending Approvals
queue.approveReject: Approve to continue, or Reject to cancel
queue.retry: Failed jobs can be retried with one click
queue.tip2: Green check = done, Blue pulse = active, Yellow shield = quarantined, Red = error.
queue.tip3: Hover over any pipeline step to see its name and description.
queue.pipelineSummaryDesc: Clique nos badges de contagem (Queued, Processing, Done, Quarantined) para expandir um painel inline com a lista de ficheiros.
queue.reprocessPopupDesc: Popup renderizado via portal para o foreground, escapando o overflow do container da tabela.

profiles.title: Profiles — Transcode Configuration
profiles.desc: Profiles define how media is transcoded. Use built-in presets for common workflows, or create custom profiles with specific codec, resolution, and quality settings.
profiles.presets: 6 system presets: Broadcast HD/SD, Web 4K/HD, Proxy, Social
profiles.custom: Create custom profiles with the editor sidebar
profiles.duplicate: Duplicate any profile as a starting point
profiles.settings: Set video codec, resolution, bitrate, audio LUFS, and VMAF threshold
profiles.tip1: System presets are read-only. Duplicate them to make changes.
profiles.tip2: Lower CPU preset = better quality but slower encoding.
profiles.tip3: The VMAF threshold determines the minimum acceptable quality score.

settings.title: Settings — Configuration
settings.desc: Configure output directory, concurrent jobs, GPU acceleration, notifications, theme, language, and more.
settings.general: General — output folder, concurrent jobs, GPU, notifications
settings.system: System — OS/hardware info, FFmpeg version, DB stats
settings.cloud: Cloud — manage cloud profiles, credentials, and browse remote files (see Cloud tab)
settings.tip1: Set your Output Directory first — this is where all processed files go.
settings.tip2: More concurrent jobs = more CPU/RAM usage. Start with 2.
settings.tip3: Factory Reset wipes everything. Export your settings first if unsure.
settings.factoryResetConfirmDesc: Factory reset com autorização explícita para apagar ficheiros. Primeiro diálogo confirma o reset; segundo pergunta se apaga os ficheiros de output.

logsTab.title: Logs Tab (v0.24.0)
logsTab.desc: Configure file logging verbosity, retention policy, and upload endpoint. View storage usage and export or clear log files.
logsTab.verbosity: Verbosity: Basic (errors only), Normal (INFO+), Debug (all + UI clicks)
logsTab.retention: Retention: set max days and max size (MB). Old logs are compressed to ZIP.
logsTab.upload: Upload logs to a developer endpoint for troubleshooting

cache.title: Cache Display (v0.24.0)
cache.desc: Monitor and manage temporary cache files created during processing.
cache.transcodeCache: Processing Cache — transcode and proxy temporary files
cache.clear: Clear cache safely (blocked if jobs are active)

shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
shortcuts.desc: Common keyboard shortcuts. Modifier key depends on your platform (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl on Windows/Linux).

cloud.title: Cloud — Destinations & File Browser
cloud.desc: Configure cloud storage destinations for automatic file delivery after transcoding. Supported providers: FTP/FTPS, SFTP, SMB, S3 (and compatible: MinIO, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, R2), Google Drive, Google Drive Personal, Dropbox, MEGA.

destinations.title: Cloud Destinations
destinations.desc: Add cloud profiles in Settings → Cloud. Each profile stores the connection details for one provider. A job can have multiple cloud destinations — the file is uploaded to all of them automatically after the job completes.
destinations.tip1: iCloud is not supported — Apple does not expose a public file API for third-party apps.
destinations.tip2: Credentials are stored locally on your device. They are never sent to any Nexora server.
destinations.tip3: Google Drive resolves folder names from base_path — it does not use internal folder IDs.

browser.title: Cloud File Browser
browser.desc: Click the Browse button (folder icon) on any cloud profile in Settings → Cloud to open the file browser. Navigate into subdirectories, select files, download them to a local folder via the native file dialog, or delete them directly from the remote storage.
browser.tip1: Select multiple files with the checkboxes on each row, then use Delete Selected or Download Selected.
browser.tip2: Download opens the native OS file picker so you choose where to save.
browser.tip3: Delete is permanent — there is no recycle bin on remote storage.

upload.title: Automatic Upload
upload.desc: When a transcoding job completes, Nexora automatically uploads the output file to all configured cloud destinations for that job. Uploads use 3 retries with exponential backoff. A failed upload is logged but does not mark the job as failed.
upload.tip1: Each job can override the default cloud destination set in Settings → Cloud.
upload.tip2: Upload progress is not shown in the UI — check the Logs tab for upload status.
upload.tip3: Google Drive upserts files: if a file with the same name exists in the destination folder, it is replaced rather than duplicated.

sftp.title: SFTP — SSH File Transfer
sftp.desc: Connect to any SFTP server with username/password or SSH key authentication. Fill in Host, Port (default 22), Username, Password or key path, and the remote base folder.
sftp.tip1: Port 22 is the standard SFTP port — change only if your server uses a custom port.
sftp.tip2: Password auth and key-based auth are both supported.
sftp.tip3: Use 'Test Connection' to verify the server is reachable and the credentials are valid before saving.

smb.title: SMB / Windows Share
smb.desc: Connect to Windows shares and NAS devices using SMB/CIFS. Enter the share path (e.g. \\server\share), username, and password. Leave username/password empty for guest access.
smb.tip2: Domain accounts: enter username as DOMAIN\user.
smb.tip3: SMB paths containing '..' are blocked for security (path traversal prevention).

gdriveOAuth.title: Google Drive — OAuth Device Flow
gdriveOAuth.desc: Authenticate Google Drive without storing passwords. Nexora uses OAuth 2.0 Device Flow with built-in credentials — no setup required on your part.
gdriveOAuth.step1: Click 'Authenticate' — Nexora requests a device code from Google
gdriveOAuth.step2: Open the provided URL in your browser and enter the user code
gdriveOAuth.step3: Nexora polls Google every 5 seconds until you authorize. The token is stored locally.

gdrivePersonal.title: Google Drive Personal — PKCE OAuth
gdrivePersonal.desc: Use your own Google Cloud Console credentials (Client ID + Client Secret). This gives you full control over the OAuth app that accesses your Drive. Nexora uses PKCE flow — no client secret is stored on disk.
gdrivePersonal.step1: Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID in Google Cloud Console (type: Desktop App)
gdrivePersonal.step2: Enter the Client ID and Client Secret in the profile form, then click 'Authenticate'
gdrivePersonal.step3: A browser window opens — log in and authorize. The token is saved in the OS keychain.

dropbox.title: Dropbox — PKCE OAuth
dropbox.desc: Use your own Dropbox App Key to connect. Create a Dropbox app at developers.dropbox.com, then enter the App Key in the profile. Nexora uses PKCE flow — your App Secret is never stored.
dropbox.step1: Go to developers.dropbox.com → Create App → Scoped Access → Full Dropbox
dropbox.step2: Copy the App Key and enter it in the Dropbox profile form
dropbox.step3: Click 'Authenticate' — a browser window opens to authorize. The token is stored in the OS keychain.

mega.title: MEGA — End-to-End Encrypted Cloud
mega.desc: Connect with your MEGA email and password. Files are always end-to-end encrypted by MEGA — Nexora never sends data in plaintext to MEGA servers. The destination folder must exist in your MEGA account before testing.
mega.tip1: Create the destination folder in mega.nz first (e.g. Nexora/Output inside Cloud Drive).
mega.tip2: Enter the folder path without a leading slash: Nexora/Output
mega.tip3: Login is performed fresh per operation — no session is cached locally.

s3.title: S3 & Compatible Providers
s3.desc: Connect to AWS S3 or S3-compatible services. Fill in Endpoint (leave blank for AWS), Bucket, Region, Access Key ID, and Secret Access Key.
s3.providers: Supported: AWS S3, MinIO, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2 (path-style endpoints)

icloud.title: iCloud Drive
icloud.desc: iCloud is supported via local folder sync. Nexora reads/writes the iCloud Drive folder on your local disk.

logs.title: Logs — Diagnostics
logs.desc: View structured application logs with filtering by level, source, and time range. Export logs for troubleshooting.
logs.filter: Filter by level (DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR), source, or time
logs.export: Export all logs to a text file for sharing
logs.levels: Red border = ERROR, Yellow border = WARN
logs.autoScroll: Auto-scroll keeps the view at the newest entries
logs.tip1: Use Ctrl+Shift+E as a shortcut to export logs.
logs.tip2: Search for specific error messages to find patterns.
logs.tip3: Clearing logs does not affect the database or jobs.

assetDetail.title: Asset Detail — File Workspace
assetDetail.desc: Asset Detail is the main workspace for a single video file. Toggle between original and processed previews, play inline, view technical metadata, and manage the file.
assetDetail.hero: Hero section with toggle Original/Processed, play button, and action bar
assetDetail.mediaInfo: MediaInfo tabs: General, Video, Audio, Subtitles, Tags, SHA-256
assetDetail.technicalAnalysis: Side-by-side technical comparison of original vs. processed
assetDetail.jobHistory: All processing jobs for this asset with pipeline stages and scores
assetDetail.tip1: Use the toggle to switch between source and output previews.
assetDetail.tip2: Click Play to watch the video inline without leaving the app.
assetDetail.tip3: The Technical Analysis tab compares codec, resolution, HDR, and more.

import.title: Import — Adding Media
import.desc: Import video files into Nexora via drag-and-drop, file dialog, or folder scan. Supported formats: MP4, MKV, MOV, MXF, AVI, WebM, TS, M2TS.
import.dragDrop: Drag video files anywhere on the window
import.fileDialog: Or click to open the native file picker
import.folderScan: Add Folder imports all supported videos from a directory
import.batchDesc: Process multiple files at once. Choose a global profile or set a different profile per file. Optionally add cloud destinations.
import.cloudPicker: Select cloud destinations for automatic upload after processing
import.tip1: Supported formats: MP4, MKV, MOV, MXF, AVI, WebM, TS, M2TS.
import.tip2: The ingest modal lets you choose between Analyze Only (metadata) or Import & Process.
import.tip3: Files with HEVC, ProRes, DNxHD, or AV1 codecs may be quarantined for manual approval.

comparator.title: Visual Comparator
comparator.desc: Compare the original and processed video side-by-side with synchronized playback, scrubbing, and adjustable divider.
comparator.splitScreen: Drag the vertical divider to reveal more of one side or the other
comparator.scrubSync: Move the timeline scrubber to navigate to any frame — both videos stay in sync
comparator.playPause: Use the Play/Pause button to toggle playback on both videos simultaneously
comparator.tip1: The comparator only appears when a processed output exists.
comparator.tip2: Both videos load from local paths via convertFileSrc for best performance.
comparator.tip3: Click the divider and drag horizontally to adjust the split between original and processed.

onboarding.title: Onboarding Wizard
onboarding.desc: At first launch, a 4-step wizard guides new users through choosing an output directory, setting preferences, and completing privacy/telemetry settings.
onboarding.tip1: Step 1: Welcome — overview of Nexora's core features.
onboarding.tip2: Step 2: Output Directory — pick where processed files will be saved.

watchFolders.title: Watch Folders
watchFolders.desc: Automatically monitor local directories for new video files. When a new file is detected and stabilised (debounced), it is automatically ingested into the Library.
watchFolders.tip1: Add folders in Settings → Watch Folders.
watchFolders.tip2: A 3-second debounce prevents ingesting incomplete/copied files.

privacy.title: Privacy & Telemetry
privacy.desc: Telemetry is opt-in and disabled by default. When enabled, Nexora collects anonymised startup events for diagnostics.
privacy.tip1: Telemetry never sends file names, paths, or any personal data.
privacy.tip2: Telemetry can be enabled/disabled at any time in Settings → Privacy.

bugReport.title: Bug Reporting
bugReport.desc: Report issues directly from the app via the orange bug icon in the TopBar. The Bug Report form lets you copy logs to clipboard or open a pre-filled GitHub issue.
bugReport.tip1: Attach recent logs (50 lines) to provide context.
bugReport.tip2: The GitHub issue link pre-fills the title and body from your report.
bugReport.tip3: Bug reports are sent to GitHub — not to any Nexora server.

platform.title: Platform-Adaptive UX (v0.25+)
platform.desc: Nexora adapts its appearance to match your operating system for a native feel.
platform.windows: Windows 11: Mica/Acrylic backdrop, Segoe UI Variable font, Fluent controls
platform.macos: macOS: NSVisualEffectView vibrancy, SF Pro font, traffic light window controls
platform.linux: Linux: Stable GTK decorations, Cantarell font, neutral window controls

security.title: Security & Privacy
security.desc: Nexora stores sensitive data securely and validates all external inputs.
security.keychain: Cloud credentials are stored in the OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service)
security.pathTraversal: Remote paths are validated to prevent directory traversal attacks
security.endpointValidation: Log upload endpoints must use http:// or https:// protocols

steps.1: Add media via drag & drop or file dialog
steps.2: Select a transcode profile (broadcast-hd, web-4k, etc.)
steps.3: Submit to the queue — jobs process automatically
steps.4: Review QC reports and approve/reject quarantined items
steps.5: Access processed files in the output folder

tipsList.1: Use GPU acceleration for 5-10x faster transcodes
tipsList.2: Enable notifications to get alerts when jobs finish
tipsList.3: Check the Logs page for detailed FFmpeg output
tipsList.4: Factory Reset wipes everything — use with caution

usage.step1Desc: Click the rocket icon in the navigation bar to access the processing page.
usage.step2Desc: Drag an MP4, MXF, MOV or any FFmpeg-supported format to the drop zone. You can also click to open the file picker.
usage.step3Desc: Choose the profile appropriate for the final destination (broadcast, web, social). Each profile has pre-configured parameters for compliance and optimal quality.
usage.step4Desc: Click Process. The job is added to the queue and processed in the background. The app remains responsive during processing.
usage.step5Desc: The Dashboard shows active jobs, average VMAF score and disk space. The progress bar updates in real time.
usage.step6Desc: After completion, the asset appears in History with codec, duration, size and VMAF score. Use the details button to see all metadata.
usage.tip1: Enable GPU in Settings for 5-10x faster transcoding
usage.tip2: The Proxy profile is ideal for creating editing versions — never for final delivery
usage.tip3: Save logs in Settings → Logs for troubleshooting
usage.tip4: The output directory can be set globally or per profile in Settings

profiles.title: Available encoding profiles

broadcastHd.name: Broadcast HD
broadcastHd.desc: Full broadcast compliance — H.264 High 4.1, 50 Mbps, -23 LUFS

webHd.name: Web HD
webHd.desc: Optimized for web and streaming — H.264, 8 Mbps

proxy.name: Proxy
proxy.desc: Fast offline editing — 720p, 2 Mbps, low latency

social.name: Social
social.desc: Social media — vertical and square formats

profiles.note: System profiles cannot be edited. Duplicate them to create custom variants.

metrics.title: Quality metrics
metrics.vmaf: VMAF (Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion) scores perceptual quality from 0-100. Thresholds: 85 (web), 90 (broadcast SD), 93 (broadcast HD/4K).
metrics.lufs: LUFS (Loudness Units Full Scale) measures audio loudness. Target: -23 LUFS for broadcast, -14 LUFS for web/social.
metrics.truePeak: True Peak (dBTP) prevents digital clipping. Limit: -1 dBTP for all profiles.
metrics.realtime: Real-time metrics update every 2 seconds during active jobs.
metrics.vmafDescription: Perceptual video quality metric developed by Netflix. Simulates human perception by comparing the processed video with the original.
metrics.lufsDescription: Integrated loudness measure according to EBU R128 standard. The standard target for European broadcast is −23 LUFS ±1 LU. For streaming (Spotify, YouTube) the target is typically −14 LUFS.
metrics.ramDesc: RAM — memory used / total in GB
metrics.networkDesc: Network ↓↑ — aggregated download and upload throughput of all interfaces

system.stackFrontend: Frontend: React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS 4 + Zustand
